_README: SustainaFund case study - every figure below is verified against the team's official method record and the raw result CSVs. DO NOT invent, round differently, or extrapolate any number. If a slide needs a number that is not in this file or in the accompanying CSVs, leave the slide without that number and flag it.
_units: All returns and risks are ANNUALISED PERCENT unless stated. 'pp' = percentage points. Ratio = expected return / expected risk (not a Sharpe ratio, risk-free rate is not subtracted).

meta.event: HTW Berlin Summer School 2026 - FICO Xpress case study

how_the_5_71_is_built: 1. Take the weights that are optimal under the LOCAL-currency covariance matrix.
2. Re-price those same weights under the USD covariance matrix to get their TRUE risk and return.
3. Solve a completely new efficient frontier using the USD covariance matrix.
4. Interpolate that new frontier at the true risk found in step 2, and subtract the true return from step 2. The gap is 5.71 pp.

validation_checks.check: adjustment ratio anchored at 1.00 at the latest date and decaying into the past
validation_checks.evidence: Unilever 0.68 -> 0.81 -> 1.00; NVDA close to 1 throughout because it pays almost no dividend

validation_checks.check: volatility essentially unchanged - a dividend adds drift, not noise
uplift ordered by sector dividend yield

expected_returns.estimator: James-Stein empirical-Bayes shrinkage applied to mu only
expected_returns.raw_estimator: mean daily log return, annualised x252
expected_returns.shrink_target_definition: a single scalar - the grand mean of raw mu over the 989 stocks with complete history
expected_returns.tuning_parameters: none - tau^2 and se_i^2 are both estimated from the data

STALE_NUMBERS_DO_NOT_USE.16.6: from an earlier data generation, before dividend adjustment and USD conversion

risk_model.form: Sigma = B F B' + diag(D), principal component factor model
risk_model.purity_note: The delivered static model uses the pure 20-factor PCA covariance. Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage is used ONLY inside the walk-forward backtest and the crisis stress test, and is never blended with the factor structure.
risk_model.selection_logic: 20 is NOT the smallest k that reaches zero error. k=5 already crosses zero, but the margin is thin and NOT monotone - k=10 falls back below zero, which shows the low-k region is measurement noise. 20 is the smallest k with a margin wide enough not to depend on which portfolio is picked.

factor_interpretation.evidence: correlation 0.996 with the equally weighted index

risk_model.explicit_region_factor_test: Adding an EXPLICIT Europe/US factor barely moved residual correlation (13.6% -> 13.1%), because PCA had already found that split by itself at F2.
risk_model.honest_line: The open question is not that factors 5 to 20 have no name. It is how much variance is left in the residual that the model treats as independent.

rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: carries 19.2% MORE true risk than the quadratic solution, and misreports its own risk by a factor of 1.64
broke the >=30 holdings counter - returned 26 real positions while reporting 30. A wrong answer that validates is worse than a slow one.

the binaries make the feasible set non-convex, so a weighted sum can only reach the convex hull and misses Pareto-optimal points. Xpress's native multi-objective needs every objective linear, which turns a 0.8s convex MIQP into an MIQCP that did not finish in 2 minutes.

model_form.mip_gap_choice: 0.1%, not 1%. At a 1% gap the measurement noise (0.078 pp) is the same size as the real effects being measured (0.042 pp).

added_by_the_team.note: not binding at Neutral (uncapped top sector is 27.10%); it binds at the minimum-risk end (uncapped 33.95%). Tightening to 20% costs 0.160 pp and binds at every profile.

added_by_the_team.sign_note: the measured effect is +0.008 pp, i.e. the floor does not cost anything - the number is inside the noise. Present it as 'effectively free', never as a real cost.
added_by_the_team.note: Floors of 20 / 30 / 40 give 14.299% / 14.300% / 14.305% at Neutral, so the level is not load-bearing. Excludes 10 stocks (0.9% of the universe), including Berkshire Hathaway at ESG 24.1.
companies whose core business is weapons and ammunition, following Norwegian sovereign-fund precedent. Treated as a compliance floor, so it is not sensitivity-tested.

diversified defence and aerospace conglomerates - RTX also makes civilian jet engines, Kongsberg has maritime and digital divisions. Genuinely contested post-2022, so it is a toggle rather than a baked-in judgement.
costs +0.112 pp of risk at matched return, or -0.067 pp of return at matched risk. Removes 11.7 pp of Swiss concentration. No level between 20% and 40% is ever infeasible.

esg_cost_decomposition.reading: the brief's own averaging constraint carries essentially the entire cost of ESG; the floor we added is nearly free

why_a_separate_weapons_screen.case: Rheinmetall carries an ESG score of 87.3 and would take 10.2% of the book with no explicit screen
why_a_separate_weapons_screen.reason: an ESG rating measures governance and disclosure quality, not what a company makes. No ESG threshold fixes this because the score is not measuring it.

constraints.data_defect_found: Four of the ten Tier-2 tickers did not exist in the dataset, so the screen was silently excluding six of ten. The dangerous one was BA.L (BAE Systems): BA.N does exist in the dataset and is BOEING, so a plausible-looking correction would have excluded the wrong company.

concentration.switzerland_rank: largest country at 14 of 15 frontier points
concentration.why_nothing_caught_it: the region cap cannot see a single country, and a sector cap cannot see a country that spans two sectors. Swiss cantonal banks and Swiss real estate are two different sectors in one small market.

us_exemption_is_forced_not_chosen.argument: the brief requires at least 40% in each region, so a country cap below 40% applied to the US is infeasible on its own
us_exemption_is_forced_not_chosen.proof: removing the exemption at a 25% cap produces an irreducible infeasible set of exactly three constraints - the budget, the Europe region cap and the US country cap - with total infeasibility 0.15, which is exactly 1 - 0.60 - 0.25

concentration.caps_are_not_substitutes: with only a country cap, one sector reaches 39.8%; with only a sector cap, Switzerland reaches 46.8%. Both are needed, or neither claim can be made.

frontier.construction: beta is swept in 15 equal steps between the global minimum-variance corner and the maximum achievable return; each step is a separate MIQP solve
frontier.esg_reading: the ESG constraint is active at every single frontier point
frontier.IMPORTANT_intermediate_points: Points 1-7, 9 and 10 are NOT in this file. Draw the frontier as a smooth monotone curve through the six exact points above and mark ONLY those six. Never print a number for an unlabelled point.

selection_rule.neutral: highest return/risk ratio on the frontier - no arbitrary target and no risk-aversion parameter to choose
selection_rule.risk_prone: highest return among NON-DEGENERATE points, where degenerate means the top three holdings exceed 40% of the budget OR more than 15 positions sit at the 1% floor

frontier.why_point_14_is_not_risk_prone: At point 14 three positions are pinned at the 20% cap, 23 of 30 positions sit at the 1% floor, and 60% of the budget is in three stocks. Its return/risk ratio of 0.779 is WORSE than the risk-averse book's 1.067 - a dominated portfolio no mandate holder would sign.
frontier.threshold_defence: Both thresholds were originally a judgement call and have since been swept over a 9x9 grid. The 40% top-3 test is inert on this frontier - it never binds. The floor count is what decides, and point 11 is selected for ANY threshold from 10 to 15. 15 also has a clean reading: every point from 8 rightward holds exactly 30 stocks, so 'more than 15 at the floor' means 'more than half the book sitting at the minimum weight' - a statement about the optimiser padding to satisfy the 30-stock count.

top_holdings_known._warning: PARTIAL. Only these are confirmed. Do not fabricate the rest of any book.

backtest.protocol: walk-forward, 3-year rolling estimation window, quarterly rebalancing, buy-and-hold in between so weights drift like a real book
backtest.estimator_used: trailing mean log return + Ledoit-Wolf shrunk sample covariance - deliberately simpler than the delivered model, so that re-running does not change the estimator and the protocol at the same time

books.minvar: minimum variance at every rebalance - validates the RISK-AVERSE end
books.mandate20: maximise return, then minimise risk while giving up at most 20% of the ACHIEVABLE maximum - the out-of-sample stand-in for Neutral
books.equal_weight: 1/N over the whole universe - the reference

backtest.why_a_relative_mandate: an absolute return target is not comparable across regimes - the same beta is easy in 2021 and infeasible in 2018 - so the profile is defined relative to what is achievable in that regime

after_10bp_costs.reading: after realistic costs the return-seeking book falls BELOW the naive benchmark

backtest.holdings_note: the mandate books hit exactly the 30-stock floor at 31 of 31 rebalances - the >=30 constraint is always binding

option_b_check.what: a cheaper protocol was proposed - split the history into three chunks and rebalance twice. It was declined, and then the objection was TESTED rather than asserted.
option_b_check.result: the same protocol with two equally defensible split dates gives delta-Sharpe +0.087 on one split and -0.244 on the other - a spread of 0.331, while the 31-rebalance answer is +0.010
option_b_check.reading: a two-rebalance protocol would have produced a confident-looking result in EITHER direction from the same data and the same code

crisis_stress_test.panel_a: the delivered portfolios held through historical crisis windows. IN-SAMPLE, because mu and Sigma were estimated over a period containing all of them. It describes the delivered book but proves nothing. Neutral beats 1/N 7 of 7 - do not present this as evidence.
crisis_stress_test.panel_b: estimate on the three years strictly BEFORE each window, re-solve, hold through. This is the actual test.
crisis_stress_test.not_testable: 2015 and 2016 windows - not enough prior history
crisis_stress_test.cherry_picking_control: the chosen windows were checked against the five worst 60-day stretches found empirically in the data, to confirm they were not selected favourably

estimation_window_instability.is_it_noise: No. Bootstrap resampling WITHIN a window converges to a stable core (top selection frequency 1.00), while cores from different windows disagree, and resampling as a remedy moves the overlap only from 0.29 to 0.31. The instability is real information about the market, not a defect to be smoothed away.
estimation_window_instability.headline: shorter windows look better and are worse - the three-year book claims 25.7% return at 7.9% risk, which is the noise in a three-year mean and the optimiser buying whatever the noise flattered

what_failed.finding: No portfolio beats the naive benchmark on risk-adjusted return
what_failed.evidence: every t-statistic sits inside +/-1.96; the whole Sharpe spread from 0.829 to 0.914 is noise. Over 7.7 years the honest answer is 'not distinguishable from the benchmark'.

what_failed.finding: The model understates its own risk out of sample, worst when it matters most
what_failed.evidence: minimum-variance book: predicted 8.78% vs 13.20% realised across the backtest, a 50.3% understatement (the method record quotes 50.4% from an unrounded realised figure - either is fine, do not print both); in crises realised/predicted for the Neutral book was 1.83x in 2018 Q4, 1.44x in 2022 and 6.71x in the COVID crash. Any risk number this model produces must be presented as a LOWER BOUND.

what_failed.finding: The portfolio is unstable across estimation windows, and it is not sampling noise
The recommended profile is not where the robustness lives
what_failed.evidence: out of sample the recommended book beats 1/N in one crisis of three, while the minimum-variance book beats it in all three. Three independent analyses - crisis stress test, walk-forward backtest, window-stability study - single out the minimum-variance end as the robust one.

the_defensible_claim.statement: Recommend on RISK, not return. No risk-adjusted edge is statistically demonstrable over 7.7 years, but the volatility and drawdown reduction at the minimum-variance end is real and repeatable. That is a stronger position at a viva than a Sharpe ratio that does not survive a t-test.

evidence.sub_period_record: lower volatility than 1/N in five of six sub-periods - the single exception is the calm 2018-2019 stretch (14.15% vs 11.87%)
evidence.crisis_record: beats 1/N in all three point-in-time crisis windows (+7.57 / +4.41 / +2.11 pp)

reproducibility.principle: every rebuild is gated against something it must reproduce, and the gate is reported next to the result

gates.gate: rewriting the group caps in a different idiom
gates.result: byte-identical LP file; all 15 frontier points re-solved with max |delta weight| = 0.000
reproduces mu to 1.7e-16 and Sigma to 1.8e-15

gates.gate: new backtest harness vs the original
new 1/N vs an independently built one

gates.result: every field matches the original; the rebuilt PDF is text-identical

defects_the_gates_caught: The deck-building script read a JSON file from /tmp that nothing in the repository wrote - every scenario number on the slides came from it, and macOS clears /tmp on reboot, so the documented rebuild command crashed on a clean checkout.
Two backtest inputs were read but never written by any script, for the same reason.

A tolerance bug: counting positions 'at the 1% floor' with a tolerance of 1e-6 reports zero where there is plainly one, because at a 0.1% MIP gap the solver leaves the smallest holding at 0.010005. The correct tolerance is 1e-5, and this feeds directly into the degeneracy test that selects Risk Prone.
reproducibility.honest_limit: The stored frontier is not bit-reproducible at its flat left-hand end - points 0 through 6 differ by up to 7.7e-5 in return and by one holding. The pre-existing code reproduces the SAME deviation exactly, so this is the 0.1% MIP gap admitting genuinely alternative optima where the frontier is nearly flat. Points 8 through 14, including the recommendation, match to the last digit.

known_limitations: ESG scores and sectors are a single present-day snapshot, so applying ESG >= 70 at a 2018 rebalance uses 2025 information - look-ahead that cannot be removed without a historical ESG panel.

The universe is today's index constituents, so it is survivorship-biased by construction: companies that failed or were delisted are absent, and realised returns are therefore optimistic for every strategy, benchmark included.
Transaction costs are measured after the fact but are not priced inside the optimiser, so the model has no incentive to prefer a cheaper rebalance.

benchmark_caveat.what_1N_is: 1/N over the WHOLE universe of 1,077 names, not an equal weighting of the selected stocks
benchmark_caveat.why_it_is_not_a_portfolio: 1/1077 = 0.093% per name, below the brief's own 1% floor, and no equal-weight portfolio over more than 100 names can satisfy that floor at all. It is a reference, not a portfolio we could have proposed.
benchmark_caveat.rebalancing_sensitivity: the choice of rebalancing moves it by 0.9 pp of CAGR - daily 15.67%, buy-and-hold 15.35%, monthly 14.80%
benchmark_caveat.screened_variants: the unscreened variants miss weighted ESG >= 70; the ESG-screened one clears ESG and then breaks the 60% region cap, because the high-ESG half of the universe is 63% European
